---
title: Flows
description: Understand flows, the primary unit of orchestrated work in Prefect.
keywords: ["flows", "orchestration", "concepts"]
---

A flow is the most basic Prefect object. It is a container for workflow logic
that lets you interact with and understand the state of your runs. Flows are
defined as Python functions decorated with `@flow`.

## Write a flow

Add the `@flow` decorator to any Python function to turn it into a flow:

```python
from prefect import flow

@flow
def my_flow():
    print("Hello from a flow!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    my_flow()
```

Each time you call the function, Prefect creates a flow run and tracks its
state.

<Note>
Flows can call other flows and tasks. See the tasks documentation to learn how
to break work into smaller, observable units.
</Note>

## Flow runs and states

Every flow call produces a flow run with an associated state (for example,
`Running`, `Completed`, or `Failed`). States let Prefect report progress, retry
failures, and surface results.

## Deploy a flow

You can run flows locally or deploy them so they run on a schedule or in
response to events. Deployments can execute on your own infrastructure or on
Prefect Cloud.

For more detail on orchestrating flows, see the
[flows documentation](/v3/concepts/flows).
